physics-killer-02.material: A vertical circular loop of radius $R=4\,\mathrm{m}$ is attached to the bottom (height $0$) of a frictionless track. A $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ object is released from rest on the track so that it goes around the loop. Use $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Which option correctly gives, in order, the minimum release height $h_{min}$ (measured from the bottom) needed to pass the top of the loop without leaving the track, and the normal force $N$ exerted by the track on the object at the top when the release height is $15\,\mathrm{m}$?
physics-killer-02.thinking.0: Work and the Interconversion of Mechanical Energy (Inquiry)
physics-killer-02.s.s1.prompt: A vertical circular loop of radius $R=4\,\mathrm{m}$ is attached to the bottom (height $0$) of a frictionless track. A $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ object is released from rest on the track so that it goes around the loop. Use $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Which option correctly gives, in order, the minimum release height $h_{min}$ (measured from the bottom) needed to pass the top of the loop without leaving the track, and the normal force $N$ exerted by the track on the object at the top when the release height is $15\,\mathrm{m}$?
physics-killer-02.s.s1.explain: Minimum condition $N=0$: $mg=mv^2/R\Rightarrow v_{top}^2=gR=40$. Energy conservation $mgh_{min}=mg(2R)+\frac12mv_{top}^2$ gives $h_{min}=2R+\dfrac{R}{2}=2.5R=10\,\mathrm{m}$. For $h=15\,\mathrm{m}$, $v_{top}^2=2g(h-2R)=2\cdot10\cdot7=140$. From $mg+N=mv^2/R$, $N=m\left(\dfrac{v^2}{R}-g\right)=2(35-10)=50\,\mathrm{N}$. Using only the height $2R=8\,\mathrm{m}$ ignores the kinetic energy (option 1); $N=mv^2/R=70\,\mathrm{N}$ ignores gravity (option 2); $90\,\mathrm{N}$ is a sign error that adds gravity (option 3).
physics-killer-02.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-killer-02.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
